title: Act IV, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: Antony, Octavius and Lepidus mark men for death, trading relatives: Lepidus's brother and Antony's nephew are condemned. Antony plans to cut costs from Caesar's will. When Lepidus leaves, Antony calls him a 'slight unmeritable man' fit only for errands, comparing him to a horse; Octavius defends him as a soldier. They plan to meet the armies of Brutus and Cassius.

context.history: In 43 BC the Second Triumvirate published proscription lists of enemies to be killed and their property seized; the orator Cicero was among the victims.

significance: The 'avengers' of Caesar prove as ruthless as the conspirators and more cynical. Antony's plan to reduce the people's legacy undercuts his funeral speech.
